findings.issue: Acronym in the headword has no phonetic; WMS is read as letters, not as a word.

findings.issue: WAN is normally read as a word /wæn/, not spelled out W-A-N; empty phonetic hides this.

findings.issue: WWW is an acronym read as three W letters; empty phonetic omits the abbreviation reading.

findings.issue: Function word has no phonetic; strong /æt/ and weak /ət/ are both needed.

findings.issue: Given /ʊ/ is not the standard vowel; beautiful is /ˈbjuːtəfəl/.
findings.context: The garden is beautiful in spring.

findings.issue: Chinese gloss is the preserve-in-a-can verb, but the example is modal can; standalone strong/weak reading is ambiguous.
Acronym with empty phonetic; CD is read as letters.

findings.issue: Empty phonetic; example 'a Chinese' means a Chinese meal, not the language/nationality in the gloss.

result.notes: Reviewed all 250 entries. No audio was supplied, so no audio claims are made. Many multiword web/tech terms have empty phonetic fields; findings focus on acronym, notation, heteronym, or clear IPA conflicts rather than every missing field or normal US/UK variant.
